newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. experts in Iraq to discuss chemical arms.
newsitem.headline: U.N. experts in Iraq to discuss chemical arms.

text.p: A team of United Nations experts arrived in Baghdad on Thursday to examine documents provided recently by Iraq on its past chemical warfare programme, a senior U.N. official said.
Goran Wallen of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) said the move was initiated by Iraq in order to address the commission's concerns over Iraqi chemical arms.

"They are nine people and headed by Russian Igor Mitrohkin...They are here to discuss chemical issues with Iraq," Wallen, director of UNSCOM's Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre in Baghdad, told Reuters.
UNSCOM is in charge of scrapping Iraq's weapons of mass destruction under the terms of the ceasefire ending the 1991 Gulf War which drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.

"The Iraqi side after carrying out its own investigation on (its) chemical weapons has submitted new documents," Wallen said. "Our chemical team together with Iraqi experts will examine these documents."
Wallen said Baghdad had agreed to start a detailed review of its chemical weapons programme during a visit to Iraq by UNSCOM's chairman Rolf Ekeus in February.
Asked if the joint discussions signalled a new spirit of cooperation between Iraq and UNSCOM, Wallen said: "This remains to be seen at the outcome of the discussions."
Ekeus, who is expected in Baghdad on April 3-5, said in his last visit that his commission still had "serious" concerns about Iraq's chemical weapons.

UNSCOM and the International Atomic Energy Agency must certify that Baghdad has no chemical, biological, ballistic or nuclear weapons before the United Nations will lift curbs on Iraqi oil exports, which were imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
But the United Nations has allowed Iraq limited oil sales sine last December worth $2 billion over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies.
Foodstuffs bought under the deal started arriving in Iraq a week ago and a U.N. source said on Wednesday the first rations would be handed out to people by the end of April.
